Tree Time Afterschool Provision
How to Book and Pay for your child's Tree Time Club Sessions
Cost from September 2025:
The cost per session is £16.00 per child from the end of the school day -5:45pm. •
If your child attends an after-school club at either the Infant or Junior Schools, and requires after school provision following the club, then the cost will be £12.00 per child. Children will be taken to the after school provision by a member of staff.
If you wish to book a place for your child to attend Tree Time Club, please log into your child's Arbor account as you can now book and pay for your Early Bird Club sessions online with your credit/debit card. When in Arbor, look for "Activities", then "Clubs", where you will find the Tree Time Club showing for you to book your child's place.
If your child attends Orchard Junior School and has not used the Tree Time Club so far this academic year, please contact the school office so that we can set your child up on the Orchard Infant School Arbor system so that you can book your place.

Absence Reporting and Attendance
If your child is unwell and unable to attend school, please call the school number below and leave a message. Alternatively, use our admin email below ensuring in both instances you provide your child's full name, a reason for the absence and their class.
adminoffice@orchard-inf.hants.sch.uk
Is your child too poorly for school or nursery? New advice will help you decide
It is always a worry when a child becomes unwell, but it is not always obvious how to care for them and whether you should keep them at home. You can now find handy NHS guidance in one place online that will help you identify a possible condition, so you can decide whether to send your child to school or nursery.
On the NHS website mentioned below, is a list of common childhood illnesses and conditions from conjunctivitis to head lice, as well as symptoms such as a high temperature and a sore throat and what these might mean. There is advice about what to do and when a child should return to education after being treated.
Visit the website via the following link: Should your child go to school or nursery today?
or go online and search for ‘0-18 should child go to school’. Please bookmark this website so it is easy to find if ever your child becomes unwell.
If you are unsure about a child’s wellbeing, please talk to your local pharmacist, call the NHS helpline on 111, or contact your GP.
Strep A and Scarlet Fever Advice
Strep A information UK Health Security Agency.pdf
If your child is due to have any non-medical absence from school, it is a legal requirement for you to submit a request for an authorised absence from school due to exceptional circumstances to the Headteacher.
To request this from the Headteacher, please complete and return the "Application form to request authorised absence for exceptional circumstances" form below. (Paper copies are available from the school office if you do not have access to a printer) These forms must be completed in advance of the absence in order for your request to be considered by the Headteacher.
Application form to request absence due to exceptional circumstances
Guidance for Parents and Carers: Penalty Notices for non attendance
Non-medical absences of 10 sessions or more that have not been authorised by the Headteacher will result in a Penalty Notice.
Additional guidance for parents/carers on attendance and behaviour can be found on the link below
Behaviour and Attendance Guidance for Parents/Carers

Speech and Language Provision
At Orchard Infant School, we recognise that early talk is the foundation for learning. Children's speech, language and communication skills underpin their ability to learn, build relationships, express themselves, and develop emotional wellbeing. Supporting these skills as early as possible helps children to thrive both in school and beyond.
We are incredibly fortunate at Orchard Infant School to have a dedicated Speech and Language Support Assistant (SaLSA), Mrs Bowen, working within our school. Our SaLSA is also a qualified teacher with over 20 years of teaching experience, bringing a wealth of knowledge and expertise to the role.
What does our Speech and Language Support Assistant do?
Our SaLSA works closely with children, families and staff to identify and support pupils who may need additional help with their speech, language or communication skills. This includes:
We believe that early identification and intervention can make a significant difference to a child's confidence, communication and future learning.
Blueberries Classroom
Children with a speech and language need at Orchard Infant School benefit from working within our designated Speech and Language classroom, The Blueberries, providing a calm, welcoming environment where targeted support can take place.
Alongside these planned intervention sessions, we recognise the importance of developing communication as part of everyday school life. Our SaLSA works alongside children within their classrooms, supporting them to develop their speech, language and communication skills in real-life learning situations.
We also make full use of our wonderful school grounds, incorporating outdoor spaces into interventions where appropriate. These natural, engaging environments encourage conversation, develop vocabulary and provide meaningful opportunities for children to practise their communication skills in a range of contexts.
If your child attends Orchard Infant School and you are concerned about your child’s speech or language comprehension, please share these concerns with your child’s class teacher, the SENDCo or SaLSA. Our SaLSA will be happy to get in touch and work alongside you.
In addition, the website: Speech and Language UK offers a free Progress Checker for parents. It asks a series of simple questions about your child and provides guidance on whether their communication skills are developing as expected. If you choose to provide your email address, you'll also receive practical tips and activities to support your child at home.

Early Bird Breakfast Club - Terms and Conditions
early bird club terms and conditions 2025 2026.pdf
What is the Early Bird Club?
The role of our Early Bird Breakfast Club is to offer a “holistic” service with a child-centred ethos in a safe environment. Our mains aims and priorities are to:-
When does the Early Bird Club run?
The Early Bird club runs Monday to Friday in term-time from 7:30am until 8:45am (except on Inset days when the club is closed).
Children must arrive by 8:15am at the latest if they require a breakfast, or by 8:20am at the latest if they do not require a breakfast.
What does it offer?
We offer child supervision and a breakfast of fruit juice, milk or water, cereal or toast and jam, and fresh fruit, to meet the Government's compulsory nutritional standards for schools. Facilities for cleaning teeth are available if required.
Who can attend?
The Early Bird Club is open to all children attending both Orchard Infant and Junior Schools. Children attending from the Junior School will be escorted across to the Junior School at the start of their school day. Children starting school in Year R must be attending school full-time and have settled in well before they can start attending.
We do have a capacity limit of available spaces, and so we recommend you block-book sessions to avoid disappointment.
How much does it Cost?
The cost per session from September 2025:
(Sessions must be booked in advance.)
How do I book?
Bookings are made under "Clubs" on the Arbor Portal or App. (see instructions above). Places must be booked and paid for in advance as places are limited to comply with adult/child ratios. We recommend booking all required sessions for each half term in one block to avoid disappointment. Unfortunately no refunds/credits can be given for your child if they do not attend for any reason (including sickness) unless there is an emergency whole school closure (ie snow day).
How do I pay?
Payment must be made online using your credit/debit card via our Arbor Portal or App when you book your session. If you are having difficulty logging into this system, please ask the school office for assistance.
If your child goes to Orchard Junior School, you must book using the Orchard Infant School Arbor Portal (Not Orchard Junior) If your Junior school child has not attended the Early Bird Club this academic year, please contact the Infant School Office and we will add your child to the Infant School Arbor so that you can then book sessions for your child.
